crop.notes: Long 1928 feature; the clipping covers the pages we hold. The article continues past them, so later sections are not held.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's John E. Wray, in a 1928 anniversary history of local prize fighting, retold Tom Allen's 1873 win over Mike McCoole on Chouteau Island and Allen's later saloon and feud-era role.

metadata.notes: Fiftieth Anniversary sports section of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, December 9, 1928. Hand transcript includes the Wray byline and 1928 copyright.

facts.fact: Allen lost the world title to McCoole on a foul in 1869 after a mob cut the ropes and intimidated the referee
Allen beat McCoole in seven rounds on Chouteau Island, near St. Louis, for the world heavyweight title, a $4,000 purse and the gate; Tom Kelly threw in the sponge for McCoole
Allen, about 170 pounds against McCoole's 220, sharpened his spikes with a file in his corner and covered $800 of a $1,000 side bet, McCoole lending him the other $200
Allen shouted to Kelly, 'Tom, it's a bloody shame to put such a man up before me, take him out'
facts.quote: Tom, it's a bloody shame to put such a man up before me—take him out.

facts.fact: With the 1873 win Allen regained the title, the only heavyweight to lose and regain it according to Wray
Allen lost his title to Joe Goss near Louisville three years after the McCoole fight
After retiring Allen kept his public house, the Champion's Rest, until his death; Wray gives the year as 1905
Allen's saloon was on Market Street east of Seventh, among the fighters' saloons around Sixth and Seventh streets
places: Market Street east of Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen opposed gloves and the Queensberry rules, declaring that no title decided under other than London prize-ring rules with the 'raw 'uns' could be a championship fight
facts.quote: no title, decided under any other than London prize-ring rules, with the 'raw 'uns,' could be considered a championship fight

facts.fact: Allen backed Artie Flint against Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Mo.; the next day he called Flint 'the bloody quitter' in an interview at his saloon

notes: Wray gives Allen's death as 1905; he died in 1903. Only facts about Tom Allen extracted. Article continues beyond held pages. Date of Flint-McManus fight is April 16, 1888 per article; the Allen interview is the next day.
